clue.text: Freeloader taking seat in procession, duke having departed

indicators.note: the seat word sits in the middle of the shortened procession word
the duke leaves, so his letter is struck out of the procession word

parts.note: a parade is a procession
to sit is to seat oneself; sit is the verb sense of seat

explanation.surface: A sponger grabs a place in a parade once the duke has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freeloader taking' may look like the definition; 'taking' is only a link, and the duke's departure leaves PARAE to hold the seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite, in the figurative sense, lives off others without contributing, exactly what a freeloader does.

clue.text: Well-mannered European drinking vermouth

indicators.note: the European swallows the vermouth, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A courteous continental sips a vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as Italian vermouth comes from the old bar order 'gin and It'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: polite and well-mannered both describe courteous behaviour.

clue.text: Fish seen round mouth of river? It's something else

indicators.note: the fish goes round the following letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish

indicators.note: the mouth of a river is where it begins, so take the first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spots a fish near a river mouth and declares it remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something else' is the idiom for an exceptional thing; the question mark hints the river letter is the odd one in.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: calling a thing 'something else' means it is extraordinary, which describes an uncommon find.

clue.text: Alone, embarrassed band

parts.note: simply can mean only or merely, as alone does in 'alone is enough'
an embarrassed person goes red in the face

explanation.surface: A solitary, red-faced musician describes their group.
explanation.walkthrough: Simply Red is a British pop and soul band led by Mick Hucknall.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Simply Red is a well-known British music group, so the clue's group word fits.

clue.text: Satirical song in chart — a fiver, boy negotiated

indicators.note: letters negotiated are worked around and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy haggles over a fiver for a mocking song that is in the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' shuffles CHART A FIVER BOY. The Vicar of Bray is an 18th-century English song mocking a clergyman who switched creeds to keep his living.
explanation.definitionFit: Title: the old English ballad lampoons a turncoat priest, so it is a satire set to music.

clue.text: Small drink following function causes rumour

indicators.note: the small drink comes after the function word in the answer

parts.note: to go is to function or work, as in 'the engine won't go'
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: A little drink at a social function sets tongues wagging.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: idle talk about other people's affairs is both rumour and tittle-tattle.

clue.text: In the past, with ruler's head, a £1 note

parts.note: once means at some time in the past

indicators.note: the head of the ruler is the word's first letter

explanation.surface: A banknote of old bearing the monarch's head.
explanation.walkthrough: A oncer is old British slang for a one-pound note, withdrawn in 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: British speakers once called a single-pound banknote by this nickname.

clue.text: Hurry up, or set point lost

indicators.note: a set point that is lost is in disarray, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tennis player is urged to speed up or lose a set point.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an order to put your foot on the accelerator means go faster.

clue.text: Model soldier, like leader of militia?

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
to dig something is slang for liking it

indicators.note: the leader of militia is its first letter

explanation.surface: A model soldier is asked whether it resembles a militia commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' and 'soldier' look like one toy figure; 'Model' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a paradigm is a typical example or pattern to follow, a model.

clue.text: What RNLI crew may do to celebrate?

definitions.text: What RNLI crew may do to celebrate?

parts.words: What RNLI crew may do to celebrate?
parts.note: the lifeboat crew literally launch their vessel, while the idiom means spend lavishly on a celebration

explanation.surface: Lifeboat volunteers mark a special occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The RNLI is the Royal National Lifeboat Institution, Britain's sea rescue charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to go to great expense for a party or treat, said literally of launching a lifeboat.

clue.text: Mailer novel about a town in Wyoming

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, that is around, the single letter
novel as an adjective means new, so the name's letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A Norman Mailer novel about a town in Wyoming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges MAILER into LARMIE, and 'about' wraps it round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Fact: Laramie is a city in south-eastern Wyoming, home of the state university.

clue.text: Not easy to make out relative, a Republican

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

explanation.surface: A relative who is a Republican is hard to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something hard to discern or understand is ambiguous or vague.

clue.text: Young child at a large comprehensive

parts.note: a tot is a small child
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A small child at a big comprehensive school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehensive' looks like a British state secondary school; here it is the adjective meaning complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: complete or all-inclusive, the adjective sense of comprehensive.

clue.text: One's golf club entertaining that female novelist

indicators.note: the letters around host the female pronoun, holding it inside

her is the pronoun for that female

explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Isherwood was the English author of Goodbye to Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Christopher Isherwood wrote the Berlin stories behind Cabaret, so he is a writer of fiction.

clue.text: Comic at the bar — card, extremely impressive

indicators.note: comic as an adjective means farcical, so the words are jumbled

parts.note: a king is a playing card

explanation.surface: A comedian in the pub is a terrific card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' rearranges AT THE BAR into BREATHTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something so impressive it leaves you gasping is stunning.

clue.text: A repair, by workers on time for a change

parts.note: to mend is to repair
men are workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: Workers fix something in good time, making an alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an amendment is a revision or alteration, as to a law or text.

clue.text: Reveal cure available

parts.note: to smoke fish or meat is to cure it
out means available, as a book that is out

explanation.surface: A cure is now on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cure' looks like a medical remedy; it is the preserving sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to drive something hidden into the open is to expose it.

clue.text: May and Johnson, perhaps, may provide answer between noon and six, if broadcast

clue.text: Tennis game, then assorted large drinks

parts.note: mixed means assorted
doubles are double measures of spirits

explanation.surface: After tennis, a round of assorted big drinks.

clue.text: A chemical that's partly unstable, a chloride

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

clue.text: Whack barrier round front of palace

clue.text: Venomous type? Man has company support

clue.text: Uncomfortably cold, reportedly, in a South American country

clue.text: Greek character dealt deviously

explanation.definitionFit: Example: the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Instrument installed in radio car in addition

clue.text: Comprehensive cover?

clue.text: One carrying out an examination on canopy

definitions.meaning: a person who checks or trials something

clue.text: Falsely incriminate small person at college after last of thefts
